# laravel_cloud_edge_network_rule (Resource)

Manages a custom rule in a ruleset (firewall, rate limit or cache) of a dedicated edge network. Rules in a ruleset are evaluated in order. An edge network takes at most 50 custom rules across its rulesets. A ruleset takes one change at a time, so a change made while another is in progress is retried for up to three minutes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "laravel_cloud_edge_networks" "mine" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

# Block the WordPress login probes.
resource "laravel_cloud_edge_network_rule" "block_wp" {
  edge_network_id = data.laravel_cloud_edge_networks.mine.edge_networks[0].id
  ruleset         = "firewall"
  name            = "Block WordPress probes"
  settings = jsonencode({
    action = "block"
    criteria_groups = [
      { criterias = [{ criteria = "value", field = "uri_path", operator = "equals", value = "/wp-login.php" }] },
      { criterias = [{ criteria = "value", field = "uri_path", operator = "equals", value = "/xmlrpc.php" }] },
    ]
  })
}

# Rate limit logins, evaluated before the firewall rule above.
resource "laravel_cloud_edge_network_rule" "login_rate_limit" {
  edge_network_id = data.laravel_cloud_edge_networks.mine.edge_networks[0].id
  ruleset         = "rate_limit"
  name            = "Throttle logins"
  settings = jsonencode({
    requests_per_period = 10
    period              = 60
    action              = "managed_challenge"
    action_duration     = 600
    throttles           = false
    criteria_groups = [{
      criterias = [
        { criteria = "value", field = "uri_path", operator = "equals", value = "/login" },
        { criteria = "value", field = "request_method", operator = "equals", value = "POST" },
      ]
    }]
  })
  position = { index = 1 }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `edge_network_id` (String) ID of a dedicated edge network, such as one from laravel_cloud_edge_networks. The shared edge network takes no custom rules. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `name` (String) Rule name, unique within the ruleset (max 100 chars).
- `ruleset` (String) Ruleset the rule belongs to: `firewall`, `rate_limit` or `cache`. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `settings` (String) The rule's action and conditions as a JSON object, usually written with jsonencode(). Its keys depend on the ruleset; GET /edge-networks/{id}/rulesets/{ruleset} lists the actions, fields and operators each accepts. Conditions go in `criteria_groups`: a request matches when every condition of at least one group matches. Keys left out take the API's defaults (such as a rate limit's `counting_key`) and are not compared, and null values are ignored.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Rule description (max 255 chars).
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the rule applies. An inactive rule keeps its position but matches no requests. Defaults to `true`.
- `position` (Attributes) Where to place the rule among the ruleset's rules: exactly one of `before`, `after` or `index`. Without it, a new rule is added last. It is applied when the rule is created and when it changes, and is not read back, so moves made outside Terraform are not detected. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--position))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Rule ID.

<a id="nestedatt--position"></a>
### Nested Schema for `position`

Optional:

- `after` (String) ID of another rule in the ruleset to place this rule after.
- `before` (String) ID of another rule in the ruleset to place this rule before.
- `index` (Number) Position in the ruleset, 1 being first.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Edge network rules are imported as "edge_network_id:ruleset:rule_id".
terraform import laravel_cloud_edge_network_rule.example edgenet-...:firewall:nru-...
```
